repo.description: ## Summary An authenticated command injection vulnerability in the GetLogs Livewire component allows users with team membership (lowest privilege `member` role) to execute arbitrary commands as root on managed servers. The `$container` Livewire public property is interpolated directly into shell commands (`docker logs`, `docker service logs`) without sanitization, and can be modified by any client via the Livewire wire protocol because it lacks the `#[Locked]` attribute. The `getLogs()` method performs **no authorization check** - it does not call `$this->authorize()` or verify the authenticated user's team owns the server or resource. Command output is returned **directly in the HTTP response** via the component's `$outputs` property, effectively giving the attacker an interactive webshell. ## Details **Vulnerable File:** `app/Livewire/Project/Shared/GetLogs.php` **Vulnerable Code (Multiple Locations)** Line 38 (unlocked public property): ```php public ?string $container = null; // No #[Locked] attribute - client-modifiable ``` Lines 136, 143, 152, 159, 203, 205, 209, 211 - `$container` interpolated directly into shell commands without `escapeshellarg()`: ```php $command = "docker logs -n {$this->numberOfLines} -t {$this->container}"; ``` The `$container` property lacks the `#[Locked]` attribute, allowing clients to overwrite it via the `updates` field in `POST /livewire/update`. The injected value is passed to the managed server via SSH using `bash -se` with a heredoc, where newline characters (`\n`) in the container name become separate command lines. `getLogs()` has no authorization check - no `$this->authorize()`, no `Server::ownedByCurrentTeam()`. Contrast with `ExecuteContainerCommand.php` in the same codebase, which validates container names with regex, verifies against running containers, and checks server ownership. ## PoC **Prerequisites:** - Coolify v4.0.0-beta.468 or earlier - Authenticated user with team membership (any role, including `member` - the lowest privilege) - At least one database, application, or service resource with a running container - Burp Suite or any HTTP proxy **Steps to reproduce:** 1. **Log in as a low-privilege team member** 2. **Switching to a Team with a Database resource (e.g., Root Team)** 3. **Navigate to the database Logs page** (e.g., `/project/{project}/environment/{env}/database/{db}/logs`). The page renders a Livewire component called `project.shared.get-logs` which automatically calls `getLogs()` via SSH to fetch container logs. The output shows up in the browser. 4. **In Burp HTTP History**, find the `POST /livewire/update` request containing `"method":"getLogs"` and `"name":"project.shared.get-logs"`. The request body contains two components, the second one is the GetLogs component with `"container":"postgresql"` in its snapshot data. **Send to Repeater.** 5. **In Burp Repeater**, modify the `updates` object in the second component of the JSON body to inject the `container` property with newline-separated commands and keep rest of the body same. ```json "updates": { "container": "postgresql 2>/dev/null\necho '===RCE-START==='\nid\nwhoami\nhostname\ncat /etc/hostname\necho '===RCE-END==='\n#" } ``` **Send the request.** The server responds with HTTP 200. The response JSON contains the RCE output **directly in the `outputs` field** of the returned Livewire snapshot: ``` "outputs":"\n...===RCE-START===\nuid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)\nroot\n942cfc343b9e\n942cfc343b9e\n===RCE-END===\n" ``` The injected commands executed as root on the managed server, and the output was returned directly in the HTTP response. **What executes on the managed server:** ```bash ssh root@server 'bash -se' << \DELIMITER docker logs -n 100 -t postgresql 2>/dev/null echo '===RCE-START===' id whoami hostname cat /etc/hostname echo '===RCE-END===' # DELIMITER ``` Each `\n` in the container name becomes a separate command line in the heredoc. ## Impact - **Remote Code Execution:** Arbitrary command execution on managed servers with output returned directly in the HTTP response - **Root Privilege:** All commands execute as root due to Coolify's SSH execution model - **Interactive Webshell:** Unlike blind injection, command output is returned in the `$this->outputs` property (line 186) of the Livewire response, giving the attacker full interactive command execution over HTTP - **Missing Authorization:** No `$this->authorize()` or `Server::ownedByCurrentTeam()` check - the component does not verify the user has permission to access the target server/resource - **Full Server Compromise:** Access to SSH private keys, database credentials, application secrets, and all data on managed infrastructure - **Lateral Movement:** Coolify stores SSH keys for every connected server, enabling pivot to all managed hosts ## Recommended Fix Add `#[Locked]` to prevent client-side modification of the container property: ```php use Livewire\Attributes\Locked; #[Locked] public ?string $container = null; ``` Validate the container name before use in shell commands, consistent with `ExecuteContainerCommand.php`: ```php if (!preg_match('/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$/', $this->container)) { $this->dispatch('error', 'Invalid container name.'); return; } ``` Add authorization and server ownership verification: ```php $server = Server::ownedByCurrentTeam()->find($this->resource->server_id); if (! $server) { $this->dispatch('error', 'Unauthorized.'); return; }
repo.summary: Authenticated Remote Code Execution in GetLogs Livewire Component
